html:
A battle fought in 740 at Akroinon, near modern Afyon in western Anatolia, in which Emperor Leo III and his son Constantine V defeated one column of a large Umayyad raiding army.

For a century Arab armies had raided Anatolia almost every year, and in 717 to 718 they had besieged Constantinople itself. In 740 the caliph Hisham sent a big expedition in several columns. The Byzantines met one of them at Akroinon and destroyed it; its commanders, including the warrior Abdallah al-Battal, were killed. Al-Battal later lived on as a hero in Arab and Turkish legend as Battal Gazi.

It was not a turning point by itself, but it was the first big Byzantine field win over the Arabs after decades of defeats. The Umayyad Caliphate soon fell into civil war, and the raids lost their force. Leo and Constantine, who opposed the veneration of icons, took the win as a sign of God's favour for their policy of iconoclasm.
